note: 20-inch gap. Put Magnus’s nearest base edge about 7 inches behind your line to deny a direct Angron turn-one charge. That does not universally deny scouting Eightbound: their full first-turn reach is 28 inches. The remaining strip beyond 8 inches back is only 4 inches deep, so do not promise a comfortable whole-army safe deployment.

Diagonal deployment: do not measure “back” only from one table edge. Stage Magnus in the right-hand rear pocket and the brick toward the lower-right. Measure shortest base-to-base distance to each actual enemy start. The examples are pulled away from the central 18-inch gap. Forward Rubrics/Spawn are deliberately more exposed; move them back if they give away an unanswerable charge.

24-inch gap. More than 2 inches behind your line denies the direct Angron charge; more than 4 inches denies a full 6-inch Scout + 10-inch move + 12-inch charge. Aim for about 5 inches to the nearest important base edge, with actual cover and an exit lane. The illustrated Magnus is 4.53 inches back. This is the easiest of these examples to give the damage pieces a distance buffer.
